title: The Farmer and His Dogs
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Farmer was snowed up in his farmstead by a severe storm, and was unable to go out and procure provisions for himself and his family. So he first killed his sheep and used them for food; then, as the storm still continued, he killed his goats; and, last of all, as the weather showed no signs of improving, he was compelled to kill his oxen and eat them. When his Dogs saw the various animals being killed and eaten in turn, they said to one another, "We had better get out of this or we shall be the next to go!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why was the Farmer snowed up in his farmstead?
options: He was recovering from an illness

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Farmer unable to do because of the storm?
options: Procure provisions for himself and his family

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which animals did the Farmer kill first?
According to the passage, which animals did the Farmer kill last, before the Dogs spoke?
According to the passage, what do the Dogs say to one another?
options: "We had better get out of this or we shall be the next to go!"
"We should ask the Farmer for more food."

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "compelled" mean in "he was compelled to kill his oxen"?
Based on the passage, why do the Dogs decide they should leave?
options: They dislike the taste of the Farmer's food
They have noticed the Farmer killing his animals in turn for food and fear they will be next
They want to find a warmer place to sleep
They have been mistreated by the Farmer's family

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: It is wise to recognize danger from a pattern before it reaches you
Farmers should never keep more animals than they can feed
Storms are more dangerous to animals than to people
Loyalty to one's owner should outweigh fear for one's own safety

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who did the Farmer need to provide for besides himself?
According to the passage, which animals were killed after the sheep?
According to the passage, what did the Farmer do with each animal he killed?
As the passage uses it, what does "provisions" mean in "procure provisions for himself and his family"?
Based on the passage, what pattern do the Dogs recognize in the order the animals were killed?
options: The Farmer killed animals starting with the ones he valued least, working toward those he needed most
The Farmer killed animals at random with no order at all
The Farmer killed only animals that were already sick
The Farmer killed animals in the order they were born

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A snowed-in Farmer kills his animals for food one by one, prompting his Dogs to fear they are next and consider fleeing
A Farmer's Dogs help him hunt for food during a storm
A Farmer refuses to harm any of his animals despite the storm
A storm destroys all of a Farmer's animals before he can eat any of them
